Name: Robert Wade Bess
Question: If you lived in the South in the 1800s, do you think you'd support slavery?
Answer: My father's ancestors lived in Hematite Virginia during the mid-1800’s, an unincorporated community in the Allegheny Mountains which was sundered by the Civil War itself. When “the Restored Government of Virginia” based in Morgantown established the boundary that would eventually become the Virginia/West Virginia border in May 13, 1862, our family basically straddled a battle line. They lived in the Confederacy, but could cross over into Union territory by simply taking a Sunday afternoon stroll following church services. We have no record of which side their sympathies lay with at the time, but these were simple mountain folk. If they had any experience with slaves and slave owners at all, it would have been through the landed gentry with their boys and maidservants who visited the Sweet Chalybeate Springs to soak in the mineral baths and take the cure. To be disarmingly colloquial, “They had no dog in this fight.” And I doubt I would have either. Because as much as I may be tempted to romanticize about how progressive I would have been in the pre bellum land of my birth, I'd have been a product of my time just like everybody else back then. Nobody's gonna hop in their TARDIS and throttle the progeny of Klara and Alois Hitler in its crib. Nobody's gonna spirit John Brown away from his assignation with the gallows of Charles Town. We have more than enough evil to contend with in the bad old here-and-now. The ruins of Sweet Chalybeate Springs, Hematite Virginia (HABS Photo, October 1974)

Question: How would a psychic or fortune teller like Miss Cleo who ripped people off be treated by other inmates in the general population in prison especially if they offered to tell them their future?
Answer: Youree Dell Harris (AKA Miss Cleo) was playing a role for PSYCHIC READERS NETWORK, and while she was eventually charged along with the owners of that company for fraudulent practices, the case against her was eventually dropped. Harris died in 2016, and as best I can tell she never spent a day in jail or prison for anything at all. But had she ever served time, I imagine she would have been quite the popular inmate, because: She would have been hotter than Martha Stewart hosting a prison spread. (word)

Question: Can I purchase a gun with DUI on my record? Class 1 misdemeanor in Virginia, I’ve already got my license back and I’m off probation but do I answer yes to the question that asks about being convicted of a misdemeanor
Answer: If you could be denied a firearms purchase in the Commonwealth of Virginia for simple DUI then half the deer hunters in the state would have to settle for bow season. The only misdemeanor convictions I'm aware of that preclude one from a firearms purchase in the Old Dominion involve domestic violence. And here in Georgia, where I live now, a second simple possession conviction can prevent you from owning a gun. So you can drive drunk, but don't beat the wife and kids or get caught with a blunt in the ashtray twice, and you can hold your head high when you walk into that licensed dealership and drop the family's grocery money on that AR clone you've had your eye on. Name: Robert Wade Bess
Question: Did you read a book in prison that blew your mind?
Answer: There was a dogeared copy of LOCKERBIE: The Tragedy of Flight 103 (St Martins Press - 1989) on the pod's utility table by the TV, among the piles of Louis L’Amour and Michael Crichton. I'd put a book order in the day after I was processed, but it took the jail librarian almost a month to fill it, so I read the plane crash book because I'm neither a particular fan of cowpokes nor Cretaceous cloning. It was early in my incarceration, and I was dealing with alcohol and opioid withdrawal as best I could in an environment where symptom mitigation was considered coddling. It was an uncomfortable read. And while Western romance and techno-thrillers may dominate the fiction selection in the male pods, true crime is the headliner in the nonfiction category. Exposés like Helter Skelter, In Cold Blood, and The Executioner’s Song — if they survive the facility's content censors — make for popular fare. But I was in a precarious psychic state myself, and in no condition emotionally to imagine living in some bucolic Scottish village, only to peer out my cottage window one evening to the sight of human viscera raining from the umber skies. …had to put it down, in fact. Inmates are rarely as tough as one might imagine. …in fact, are far more human than one might think.
